why: the service loses webhooks when it restarts

payload.title: How should the service retry failed webhook deliveries so none is lost across a restart?

why: the retry design decides whether a restart can lose a delivery

payload.title: Durable outbox table, retry worker
payload.body: Write each delivery to a durable outbox table in the same transaction as the business change. A retry worker reads the table, delivers, and marks each row when the receiver answers.

why: a rival design for the retries

payload.title: Redis delayed queue, AOF everysec
payload.body: Keep pending deliveries in a Redis sorted set scored by the next attempt time, on a Redis server with appendonly yes and appendfsync everysec, drained by a retry worker.

why: a rival design for the retries

payload.title: In-process retry, persisted attempt log
payload.body: Retry inside the web process with a timer per delivery, and write every attempt to a persisted attempt log on local disk, replayed at start-up to rebuild the pending set.

why: a rival design for the retries

payload.title: Managed broker, at-most-once delivery
payload.body: Publish each delivery to a managed broker queue, with consumers on at-most-once delivery: a message is removed from the queue when it is handed to the consumer.

why: a rival design for the retries

payload.observation: Every one of the 500 webhooks arrived despite the worker kill; none missing, and 37 repeats were dropped by the receiver. Only a score of webhooks took the Redis route, not enough for a judgement.
